Summary adjusted with SLOOS insights:
- Core FOMC message is moderately positive: labor market strengthening, growth moderate, inflation near 2%, balanced risks, and policy still accommodative despite a rate hike with an outlook for gradual increases.
- SLOOS signals are mixed and temper the outlook slightly:
  - Easing: Banks expect to ease standards for C&I loans and some residential mortgages (including GSE-eligible and nonconforming jumbo), with some improvement expected in C&I and certain mortgage asset quality.
  - Tightening/risks: Banks and foreign banks expect tighter standards for CRE, construction/land development, and auto loans; foreign banks also see tighter C&I for small firms. Asset quality is expected to deteriorate in auto, credit cards, and multifamily, with weaker business loan demand reported by foreign banks.
- Net effect: Easing in business and mortgage credit supports the FOMC’s constructive view, but anticipated tightening and deteriorating asset quality in CRE/consumer credit add headwinds. Overall tone remains moderately positive but slightly less upbeat.
